arxiv-1610-03685.title: Smallest C 2 ​ ℓ + 1 C_{2\ell+1} -critical graphs of odd-girth 2 ​ k + 1 2k+1 Thanks: This work is supported by the IFCAM project Applications of graph homomorphisms (MA/IFCAM/18/39) and by the ANR project HOSIGRA (ANR-17-CE40-0022). The second author was partially financed by the French government
arxiv-1610-03685.creator: Laurent Beaudou, Florent Foucaud, Reza Naserasr
arxiv-1610-03685.description: Abstract Given a graph H H , a graph G G is called H H -critical if G G does not admit a homomorphism to H H , but any proper subgraph of G G does. Observe that K k − 1 K_{k-1} -critical graphs are the standard k k -(colour)-critical graphs.

arxiv-1707-02687.title: Robust Edge States in Amorphous Gyromagnetic Photonic Lattices
arxiv-1707-02687.creator: Shampy Mansha, Y. D. Chong
arxiv-1707-02687.description: Abstract We numerically study amorphous analogues of a two-dimensional photonic Chern insulator. The amorphous lattices consist of gyromagnetic rods that break time-reversal symmetry, with the lattice sites generated by a close-packing algorithm. The level of short-range order is adjustable, and there is no long-range order.

arxiv-1905-00322.title: Multi-level Encoder-Decoder Architectures for Image Restoration
arxiv-1905-00322.creator: Indra Deep Mastan, Shanmuganathan Raman
arxiv-1905-00322.description: Abstract Many real-world solutions for image restoration are learning-free and based on handcrafted image priors such as self-similarity. Recently, deep-learning methods that use training data, have achieved state-of-the-art results in various image restoration tasks (e.g., super-resolution and inpainting). Ulyanov et al. bridge the gap between these two families of methods in Ulyanov2018CVPR .

arxiv-2101-04499.title: Thermal state quantum key distribution
arxiv-2101-04499.creator: A Walton, A Ghesquière, G. Brumpton, D Jennings, B Varcoe
arxiv-2101-04499.description: Abstract We analyse a central broadcast continuous variable quantum key distribution protocol in which a beam produced by a thermal source is used to create a secret key between two parties, Alice and Bob. A beam splitter divides the initial beam into a pair of output beams, which are sent to Alice and Bob, with Eve intercepting Bob’s beam.

arxiv-2107-01029.title: Words in Random Binary Sequences I
arxiv-2107-01029.description: Abstract 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification 05A15, 60C05 Acknowledgement: This paper originated with the project “Fibonacci and the Gambler’s Ruin” that was offered at Louisiana State University’s 2020 Virtual Summer Math Circle program for high school students. The authors thank the LSU Math Circle program for this opportunity.

arxiv-2107-09498.title: Topological pump and bulk-edge-correspondence in an extended Bose-Hubbard model
arxiv-2107-09498.creator: Yoshihito Kuno, Yasuhiro Hatsugai
arxiv-2107-09498.description: Abstract An extended Bose-Hubbard model (EBHM) with three- and four-body constraints can be feasible in cold atoms in an optical lattice. A rich phase structure including various symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases is obtained numerically with suitable parameter settings and particle filling.

arxiv-2112-13899.title: Improvements to the Search for Cosmic Dawn Using the Long Wavelength Array
arxiv-2112-13899.creator: Christopher DiLullo, Jayce Dowell, Gregory B. Taylor
arxiv-2112-13899.description: Abstract We present recent improvements to the search for the global Cosmic Dawn signature using the Long Wavelength Array station located on the Sevilleta National Wildlife Refuge in New Mexico, USA (LWA–SV). These improvements are both in the methodology of the experiment and the hardware of the station.

arxiv-2204-12861.title: Spectral dynamics of guided edge removals and identifying transient amplifiers for death-Birth updating
arxiv-2204-12861.creator: Hendrik Richter
arxiv-2204-12861.description: Abstract The paper deals with two interrelated topics, identifying transient amplifiers in an iterative process and analyzing the process by its spectral dynamics, which is the change in the graph spectra by edge manipulations. Transient amplifiers are networks representing population structures which shift the balance between natural selection and random drift.

arxiv-2210-04425.title: Mixed neutron-star-plus-wormhole systems: Rotating configurations
arxiv-2210-04425.creator: Vladimir Dzhunushaliev, Vladimir Folomeev, Burkhard Kleihaus, Jutta Kunz
arxiv-2210-04425.description: Abstract We present rapidly rotating neutron stars featuring wormholes in their centers. They arise in general relativity in the presence of a ghost scalar field. The nuclear matter is described by a polytropic equation of state, yielding realistic masses and radii for the neutron stars. The wormholes possess small circumferential radii of size up to 3 km.

arxiv-2403-13566.title: Investigating model influence on the analytical resolution of neutron reflectometry
arxiv-2403-13566.creator: Luke A
arxiv-2403-13566.description: Abstract Neutron reflectometry is a critical tool for investigating the structure of thin films and interfaces. However, the misapplication of the Born approximation to reflection geometry leads some to assume that the minimum thickness that may be probed by neutron reflectometry is limited by the Q Q -range of the measurement.

arxiv-2411-19598.title: Channel Access Strategies for Control-Communication Co-Designed Networks
arxiv-2411-19598.creator: Gourab Ghatak, Geethu Joseph, Chen Quan
arxiv-2411-19598.description: Abstract We develop a framework for communication-control co-design in a wireless networked control system with multiple geographically separated controllers and controlled systems, modeled via a Poisson point process. Each controlled system consists of an actuator, plant, and sensor. Controllers receive state estimates from sensors and design control inputs, which are sent to actuators over a shared wireless channel, causing interference.

arxiv-2504-21121.title: Focusing of Relativistic Electron Beams With Permanent Magnetic Solenoid
arxiv-2504-21121.creator: T. Xu, C. J. R. Duncan, P. Denham, B. H. Schaap, A. Kulkarni, D. Garcia, S. D. Anderson, P. Musumeci, R. J. England
arxiv-2504-21121.description: Abstract Achieving strong focusing of MeV electron beams is a critical requirement for advanced beam applications such as compact laboratory X-ray sources, high gradient accelerators, and ultrafast electron scattering instrumentation. To address these needs, a compact radially magnetized permanent magnetic solenoid (PMS) has been designed, fabricated, and tested.

arxiv-2505-10168.title: Space-Time Multigrid Methods Suitable for Topology Optimisation of Transient Heat Conduction
arxiv-2505-10168.creator: Magnus Appel, Joe Alexandersen
arxiv-2505-10168.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Magnus Appel, Joe Alexandersen. This paper presents Space-Time MultiGrid (STMG) methods which are suitable for performing topology optimisation of transient heat conduction problems. The proposed methods use a pointwise smoother and uniform Cartesian space-time meshes. For problems with high contrast in the diffusivity, it was found that it is beneficial to define a coarsening strategy based on the geometric mean of the minimum and maximum diffusivity. However, other coarsening strategies may be better for other smoothers.

arxiv-2601-19898.title: DuwatBench: Bridging Language and Visual Heritage through an Arabic Calligraphy Benchmark for Multimodal Understanding
arxiv-2601-19898.creator: Shubham Patle, Sara Ghaboura, Hania Tariq, Mohammad Usman Khan, Omkar Thawakar, Rao Muhammad Anwer, Salman Khan, Mohamed bin Zayed University of AI, NUCES, NUST, Australian National University{shubham.patle, sara.ghaboura, omkar.thawakar}@mbzuai.ac.ae https://mbzuai-oryx.github.io/DuwatBench/
arxiv-2601-19898.description: Abstract Arabic calligraphy represents one of the richest visual traditions of the Arabic language, blending linguistic meaning with artistic form. Although multimodal models have advanced across languages, their ability to process Arabic script, especially in artistic and stylized calligraphic forms, remains largely unexplored.

pmc-10737728.title: HEARING LOSS AS A MODIFIABLE RISK FACTOR FOR DEMENTIA IN UK BIOBANK
pmc-10737728.creator: Jure Mur, Anja Leist
pmc-10737728.description: Age-related hearing loss is a predictor of cognitive impairment and dementia. The mechanisms of the observed associations are unclear but could involve depletion of cognitive reserve, the occupation of cognitive resources, and lack of sensory input to the brain. Hearing loss may therefore represent a preventable or treatable causative risk factor for dementia.

pmc-11388662.description: Graphical abstractKeywords: Ultrasonic treatment, Glutinous rice, Microbial inactivation, Starch physiochemical properties, Sweet dumplings Introduction Sticky rice, also known as glutinous rice or sweet rice, is traditionally used as a staple food for Asians because of its soft texture, high viscosity, unique flavor, and high nutritional value [1].

pmc-11555639.title: Wildfire Seasons, Prenatal PM2.5 Exposure, and Respiratory Infections by Age 1 Year: A Population-Based Case-Control Analysis of Critical Developmental Windows
pmc-11555639.creator: Qingyi Lan, Kate Weinberger, Sabrina Luke, Eric Lavigne, Scott Weichenthal, Sarah B. Henderson
pmc-11555639.description: The 2017 and 2018 wildfire seasons in British Columbia (BC), Canada were unprecedented. Among all the pollutants in wildfire smoke, fine particulate matter (PM2.5) poses the most significant risk to human health. There is limited research on prenatal wildfire smoke exposure and its impacts on infant health.

pmc-11647138.title: Deep learning model for diagnosis of venous thrombosis from lower extremity peripheral ultrasound imaging
pmc-11647138.creator: Po-Wei Chen, Bor-Yann Tseng, Zhu-Han Yang, Chi-Hua Yu, Keng-Tse Lin, Jhen-Nong Chen, Ping-Yen Liu
pmc-11647138.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). SummaryDeep vein thrombosis (DVT) causes significant healthcare burdens worldwide. This study aims to establish a deep learning model for the diagnosis of DVT from the assessment of vein compressibility. Considering the complexity of ultrasound images, convolutional neural networks with UNet and residual neural network (ResNet) are established for image segmentation, from venous duplex ultrasonographic video images, obtained through standard and portable handheld ultrasound methods.

pmc-12617235.creator: S Lioliou, K Vagionaki, N Bitsakos, G Markakis, M Papadakaki
pmc-12617235.description: BackgroundParents play a central role in recognizing early signs of attentional and behavioral difficulties that may affect their child’s wellbeing and safety. Within the framework of the Hellenic Mediterranean University’s Mobile Unit for Learning Disabilities Assessment in Crete (MIS 5162111, 2020–2023), such observations were frequently reported during clinical interviews.

pmc-13216611.title: Progressive release of long-stored carbon from tropical peatland disturbances
pmc-13216611.creator: Jun Koarashi, Masayuki Itoh, Mariko Atarashi-Andoh, Yoko Saito-Kokubu, Makoto Matsueda, Kitso Kusin, Adi Jaya, Salampak Dohong, Takashi Hirano
pmc-13216611.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Tropical peatlands are globally important, millennia-old carbon sinks, yet unprecedented human-driven degradation is triggering alarming carbon emissions. Comprehensive quantification of carbon dynamics across the disturbance sequence—from peat swamp forests to drained and fire-impacted peatlands—remains a critical knowledge gap. Here we show that over 18 years (1996–2014), drainage and subsequent peat fires released approximately 30–41 kg C m−2 from peatlands in Central Kalimantan, Indonesia, using radiocarbon dating of peat profiles and groundwater dissolved organic carbon.

pmc-13299492.title: Molecular Evidence for the Parallel Evolution of Anosmia in Multiple Odontoceti (Toothed Whales) Clades
pmc-13299492.creator: Mark S. Springer, Michael R. McGowen, John Gatesy
pmc-13299492.description: Background/Objectives. Living odontocetes are the only extant mammals that lack anatomical features associated with olfaction. A leading hypothesis for the presumed complete loss of smell (i.e., anosmia) in odontocetes is that olfaction was lost in the common ancestor of the crown clade. An alternative hypothesis is that olfaction was lost in parallel in different odontocete lineages. Methods.
